description:
This map displays an aerial false-colour infrared image of a peri-urban area in Malaga, Spain, illustrating land cover classifications. The image shows healthy vegetation in vibrant red, bare ground or sparse vegetation in reddish-brown, artificial surfaces in shades of grey, and water bodies in dark blue.

The central feature is a large, elongated area outlined in blue-cyan and labelled "1320", representing "Land without current use". This area appears as a cleared or fallow reddish-brown parcel, consistent with a "brownfield" or "wasteland" designation. Surrounding this area are other classified land cover types, likely following Urban Atlas (UA) or CORINE Land Cover (CLC) classification codes:
- To the east (right), a complex of buildings and associated grey artificial surfaces is labelled "1120" (Discontinuous urban fabric).
- Adjacent to, and partially encompassing, the "Land without current use" are areas labelled "1210" (Industrial or commercial units), characterised by clusters of buildings and paved surfaces.
- To the west (left), an area of dense, healthy red vegetation is labelled "1400" (likely Green urban areas or similar natural/semi-natural vegetation).
A thin yellow boundary encloses the overall depicted area. A body of water is visible in the bottom right corner.
